items.subject: LLMjacking: AI Model Hijacking Reaches Black Market Scale
items.what_happened: CSA research documents LLMjacking, where stolen credentials for LLM API endpoints are resold on black markets to run inference on someone else's infrastructure at their cost. Operators exposing self-hosted inference endpoints (vLLM, Ollama, TGI) should verify authentication is enforced, rotate leaked keys, and monitor for unexpected token consumption or unfamiliar client traffic.
items.why_it_matters: Classified as breaking for on-prem operators: action may be required on llm-inference-server, api-keys
items.rationale: Assess exposure before the next upgrade window

items.subject: The smallest edge AI device for local LLMs
items.what_happened: A vendor site markets a compact edge AI device for running LLMs locally. No verifiable specs, model support, or inference stack details are provided in the item, so operators cannot yet assess memory capacity, throughput, or compatibility with vLLM/llama.cpp/Ollama.
items.why_it_matters: A newly launched platform is a hardware-catalog candidate; specs enter the catalog only with a verifiable source
items.rationale: Review for the device catalog (curation stays human)
